ownership_reason: CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches owns the fault. Its javadoc defines thisStart as 'the index to start on the cs CharSequence' and start as 'the index to start on the substring CharSequence', and its own String branch forwards both unchanged to String.regionMatches(ignoreCase, thisStart, substring, start, length). Its non-String branch, taken whenever cs or substring is not a String (here the trigger's StrBuilder), initialises the cs cursor index1 from start instead of thisStart, so thisStart is never read on that branch and the substring is always compared with cs from offset start (0 for every caller). Both conjuncts of the trigger call it with thisStart > 0 and start == 0: containsIgnoreCase passes its loop index i, and endsWithIgnoreCase -> endsWith passes strOffset = str.length() - suffix.length(); both therefore compare 'report' / '.txt' with the leading characters of 'Quarterly-Report.TXT' and return false, so the boolean assertion fails. The competing suspects are correct: the caller code does not depend on the CharSequence type, and the same callers with String arguments (String branch, which honours thisStart) pass StringUtilsEqualsIndexOfTest::testContainsIgnoreCase_StringString and StringUtilsStartsEndsWithTest::testEndsWithIgnoreCase; StrBuilder.charAt is covered by StrBuilderTest::testCharAt, and builder inputs already work on the non-String branch when thisStart == start == 0 (StringUtilsStartsEndsWithTest::testStartsWithAny with a StrBuilder). Restoring index1 = thisStart repairs both conjuncts; no one-line change to a single caller or to StrBuilder repairs both.
